records.semantics: endbr64; push rbp, rbx; out1 (%rdx) is saved in %rbp, out2 (%rcx) in %rbx; sub $0x8, %rsp keeps the stack 16-byte aligned for the call; call 0x61deab0 at 0x61c3dc0 (E8 rel32 0x1aceb, the only call in the body); the callee returns the 128-bit hash as low64 in %rax and high64 in %rdx; mov %rdx, 0x0(%rbp) stores high64 through out1, mov %rax, (%rbx) stores low64 through out2; add $0x8, %rsp; pop rbx, rbp; a single ret at 0x61c3dd2. No canary, no other branch, no memory access besides the two stores.

records.method: whole-.text scan of work/hl-node-115.bin (.text va 0x1419300..0x63f6a00, file offset va - 0x1000) for E8/E9 rel32 transfers targeting 0x61c3db0 or 0x61c3de0, plus a scan for rip-relative lea instructions resolving to either address; each candidate was verified by disassembling the surrounding bytes with objdump
records.observation: exactly TWO direct call sites target the unseeded wrapper 0x61c3db0: 0x602e9bd in rocksdb::GenerateRawUniqueId (census node115-vendor-602e650, FDE 0x602e650..0x602ea44) and 0x61b01c1 in rocksdb::GetSstInternalUniqueId (census node115-vendor-61affe0, FDE 0x61affe0..0x61b0260). Exactly ONE direct call site targets the seeded wrapper 0x61c3de0: 0x61b016d, also in rocksdb::GetSstInternalUniqueId. No lea instruction anywhere in .text takes either wrapper address, so there is no function-pointer or vtable use. Indirect calls through registers cannot be seen by this scan, so a hidden indirect caller is not ruled out — recorded as a limit, not as evidence of one.

in rocksdb::GenerateRawUniqueId the call setup is: rdi = lea 0x30(%rsp) (a 168-byte stack buffer), rsi = 0xa8 (168, the length), rdx = %rbp (out1), rcx = %r12 (out2). So the raw unique ID is the 128-bit hash of a 168-byte stack buffer under the default secret and seed 0, split as high64 into *rbp and low64 into *r12. The contents of that 168-byte buffer are not established by this packet (the buffer is filled earlier in the caller, outside the window read here). Note the length 168 exceeds the 0..128 branch reconstructed in the XXH3_128bits packet; the entry point's 129..240 branch is reconstructed in the merged len_129to240_128b packet, so the delegated hash is covered for this length.

in rocksdb::GetSstInternalUniqueId the seeded call setup is: rdi = (%r12) (data pointer from the caller's input struct), rsi = 0x8(%r12) (length), rdx = 0x20(%rsp) (seed), rcx = lea 0x30(%rsp) (out1), r8 = %r15 (out2). Immediately after the call the high64 stored at rsp+0x30 is xored into %rbp (xor 0x30(%rsp), %rbp at 0x61b0172) and stored at +8 of the output UniqueIdPtr at %r13 (mov %rbp, 0x8(%r13) at 0x61b0177); the +0 slot of that struct was stored just before the call from 0x28(%rsp). The low64 goes to *r15, whose target is not followed in this packet.

in rocksdb::GetSstInternalUniqueId the unseeded call setup is: rdi = (%rsi) where %rsi = 0x8(%rsp) (data pointer), rsi = 0x8(%rsi) (length from the same struct), rdx = 0x10(%rsp) (out1), rcx = 0x18(%rsp) (out2). This site sits in the loop-back block at 0x61b01a8, reached when the byte at 0x40(%rsp) is nonzero; after the call the flag at 0x28(%rsp) is tested and control returns to 0x61b013f, so the wrapper is called once per loop iteration with the same out-pointers. Which iteration's values survive is not established by this packet.

records.status: whether an indirect caller of either wrapper exists is not established by the direct-call scan. The contents of the 168-byte stack buffer hashed at 0x602e9bd, the target of the seeded wrapper's out2 pointer %r15 at 0x61b016d, and which loop iteration's values survive at 0x61b01c1 are not established.
